question: What is the standard intravenous induction dose of propofol in a healthy adult (ASA I) patient?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is too low; sub-anaesthetic doses cause inadequate induction and risk awareness.
Correct. Propofol 1.5–2.5 mg/kg IV is the standard induction dose in healthy adults; elderly and high-risk patients require dose reduction.
This dose is excessive and risks profound cardiovascular depression, particularly hypotension.
This far exceeds safe limits and would cause severe cardiovascular and respiratory depression.

overallFeedback.feedback: The standard propofol induction dose is 1.5–2.5 mg/kg IV in healthy adults; reduce by 30–50% in elderly or high-risk patients.
Well done. Always express anaesthetic drug doses in mg/kg, not fixed volumes — body weight determines dose.
